note: Curated questions from the human-reviewed benchmark. Observations describe the recorded runs and were written after recording; they never change the recorded output.

questions.title: A direct policy lookup
questions.why: A simple single-fact question both modes should handle.
questions.observation: Both modes give the correct 60-dollar allowance with a citation. The agent's verifier judged its single claim supported.

questions.title: Comparing two policy versions
questions.why: Needs evidence from both the 2023 and 2024 travel policies.
questions.observation: Both modes give the correct change from 45 to 60 dollars. The agent cited only the 2024 passage for both figures, so its deterministic check flagged the 2023 figure as missing from the citation: the answer is right, the citation incomplete.

questions.title: A rule that changed in two ways
questions.why: Both the threshold and the approver changed between versions.
questions.observation: Standard RAG gets the thresholds right but wrongly says approval above 250 dollars was removed. The agent states both changes correctly, but cites the opening passage of each policy rather than the hotel passage, so its check flags the figures as not found in the cited text.

questions.title: Conflicting documents
questions.why: A later addendum changes the Handbook only for some employees.
questions.observation: Standard RAG says the Handbook limit is not specified, although the two-day limit was retrieved. The agent gives the correct two days with manager agreement, then adds an unnecessary hedge; its claim check did not confirm the claims.

questions.title: The two-column page regression
questions.why: The under-21 rule sits next to the over-21 rule on a two-column PDF page; the original code misread it.
questions.observation: Both modes give the correct under-21 range (0.02 to 0.07 percent, six-month suspension) from the two-column page. The planner routed this as a simple question, so the agent did not run claim verification.

questions.title: Partly answerable
questions.why: The documents give the match but not the vesting schedule.
questions.observation: Both modes give the 4 percent match and say the vesting schedule is not described. The agent adds a note that this is based on the passages retrieved.

questions.title: Not in the documents
questions.why: The right behaviour is to decline.
questions.observation: Both modes decline. The agent took the simple route, so the refusal was not separately checked.

questions.title: A false premise
questions.why: The question assumes a reduction; the allowance actually increased.
questions.observation: Known limitation: both modes accept the false premise and say the allowance was 'reduced from $45 to $60'. The agent's verifier flagged problems but did not correct the premise.

questions.title: Combining two documents
questions.why: The full answer needs the IT Security Policy and the Remote Work Addendum.
questions.observation: Known limitation: both modes give only the reporting rule and omit that home-used laptops stay under the IT Security Policy. The planner routed this as a simple question.

questions.title: A two-step question
questions.why: Two conditions from the same addendum must both be applied.
questions.observation: Standard RAG answers no and explains the country restriction. The agent reaches a hedged answer that it is 'unclear', and its text begins with an artefact ('I'll provide a revised answer') from the refinement round.
